definitions.explanation: Doing or expressing something in an undisguised, obvious way, often with a negative connotation suggesting a lack of tact or subtlety.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{露骨|ろこつ}に{嫌|いや}な{顔|かお}をした。
{露骨|ろこつ}に{無視|むし}されて{傷|きず}ついた。
examples.english: I was hurt by being blatantly ignored.

examples.japanese: あの{店員|てんいん}は{客|きゃく}によって{露骨|ろこつ}に{態度|たいど}を{変|か}えるので{評判|ひょうばん}が{悪|わる}い。
examples.english: That shop clerk has a bad reputation because they blatantly change their attitude depending on the customer.

notes: Usually carries a negative or critical nuance, suggesting the person is being too obvious or lacking in social grace. Common collocations include {露骨|ろこつ}に{嫌|いや}がる (to openly show dislike), {露骨|ろこつ}な{態度|たいど} (a blatant attitude), and {露骨|ろこつ}な{表現|ひょうげん} (explicit expression). The な-adjective form {露骨|ろこつ}な is equally common. Can also describe sexually explicit content: {露骨|ろこつ}な{描写|びょうしゃ} (explicit depiction).
